tasks.short: Coordinate fitting and alignment of heavy parts with colleagues, check the status of repair parts with stores and shops, and note handovers on the job card.

steps.what: Aircraft mechanic communicates with other workers to coordinate fitting and alignment of heavy parts
Stores and shop staff update each repair part's status in the maintenance system
Aircraft mechanic phones stores and shops to facilitate processing of repair parts
Aircraft mechanic notes handovers: on the paper job card today, on the electronic job card after the change

tasks.design: The status of each repair part (in stores, at the shop, in transit) shows on the electronic job card in the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the mechanic phones only when something is late. Shift handovers are noted on the electronic job card. Coordinating fitting and alignment on the floor stays with the mechanic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Part status was found by phoning and handovers written on paper job cards.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems show part status on electronic job cards.
tasks.still_hard: Shops outside the system do not update status.
tasks.human_edge: Guiding a heavy part into place with a colleague by eye and hand signals.

reach.learn: Whether calls about part status fall.

evidence.claim: AMOS creates and completes job cards electronically with signatures, keeping the repair log digital.
If log time stamps are used to watch technician speed, works council consent comes first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work package to the handover noted; part repairs in shops are outside.
Input contract: stores and shops update part status; fallback is phone.

Fitting, alignment and handover notes keep their full time; a handover note is a first record. s2 keeps 40 for phoning about late parts. The stores and shop updates are step s1b (share 1, other role).

incremental.description: Aircraft mechanic checks part status before starting a task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: shops often do not update part status, so most calls stay (3.3); high: stores and shops keep status current (11.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check hangar stock, look up part numbers, fill requisitions, check them, send them to stores, and collect parts and check their certificates.

steps.what: Aircraft mechanic inventories consumables in the hangar store
Aircraft mechanic looks up part numbers in the illustrated parts catalogue
Aircraft mechanic requisitions parts, materials and equipment on paper forms
Aircraft mechanic checks the final requisition: parts, quantities and that each part fits the task and the aircraft
Aircraft mechanic releases the checked requisition to stores: handed in on paper today, in the maintenance system after the change
Aircraft mechanic collects parts and checks their release certificates

tasks.design: Each electronic job card in the maintenance system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) links to the parts catalogue for that task and proposes the parts list, so the mechanic builds the requisition from the job card instead of a paper form. Hangar consumables are scanned against stock levels. Once the mechanic has checked the requisition, the mechanic releases it once to stores in the system. Checking release certificates on collection stays with the mechanic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Part numbers were copied from the catalogue onto paper forms walked to stores.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems link job cards to parts catalogues and stores.
tasks.still_hard: Parts for unplanned defects are not on the planned list.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a release certificate that does not match the part.
tasks.altitude: The mechanic checks proposed lists instead of copying part numbers.

evidence.claim: AMOS creates and completes job cards electronically.
Part-145 requires detailed maintenance records kept for 3 years, protected from damage, alteration and theft.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work package to parts received; purchasing from vendors is outside.
Input contract: catalogue links set up by engineering; fallback is paper forms.

Checking the requisition and certificates stays with the mechanic and keeps its full time. s1 keeps 60 because the mechanic still scans consumables taken and checks the shelves; s2 keeps 60 for checking the proposed parts; s3 keeps 20 for adjusting the list; s5 keeps 20 for the release.
Stores handle system requisitions as they did paper ones.

incremental.description: Aircraft mechanic adds parts for unplanned defects by hand.

approvals.approved_version: The requisition with parts and quantities exactly as checked by the mechanic in s4, released once to stores in the maintenance system for that job card; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly unplanned defects, so proposed parts lists rarely fit and parts are still looked up and listed by hand (23.0); high: planned checks with standard parts lists (41.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read engineering orders and technical publications, modify the aircraft structure or system, record the work on the job card, and sign it off.

steps.what: Aircraft mechanic reads drawings, engineering orders and technical publications
Aircraft mechanic modifies aircraft structures, systems or components
Aircraft mechanic records the work on the paper job card
Aircraft mechanic signs off the modification

tasks.design: The electronic job card ({OPS_SYSTEM}) links to the engineering order and the current revision of each technical publication, so the mechanic does not search binders or check revision status by hand. The work is recorded on the job card with mandatory fields for part and serial numbers checked against the fleet record, and signed electronically. Doing the modification and signing it off stay with the mechanic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Publications were searched in binders and work written on paper job cards re-typed at base.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems link job cards to current publications and take electronic signatures.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a drawing does not match the aircraft in front of them.

evidence.claim: AMOS completes job cards electronically and signs them through a PDF overlay.
Part-145 requires detailed maintenance records kept for 3 years with backups stored elsewhere.

assumptions: Boundary: from the engineering order to the modification signed; certifying release to service is outside.
Input contract: publications loaded and revised by technical records; fallback is binders and paper cards.
Modifying and signing off stay with the mechanic.
The authority accepts electronic signatures under the approved exposition.
s3 is the first record of the work on the job card and keeps its full time; transferring it to the repair log is cut in sibling task 9948.
research_questions: Do record errors found at audit fall?

incremental.description: Aircraft mechanic reports missing publication links.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: publications for older types are not yet loaded, so binders are still searched (2.0); high: current publications linked to every job card (7.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor aircraft systems in flight, make in-flight adjustments and corrections, and write findings in the technical log.

steps.what: Aircraft mechanic accompanies aircraft on flights and monitors systems
Aircraft mechanic makes in-flight adjustments and corrections
Aircraft mechanic writes findings in the paper technical log

tasks.design: Findings go into an electronic technical log on a tablet ({OPS_SYSTEM}) that feeds the maintenance system directly, instead of a paper log re-typed at base. Monitoring and adjusting in flight stay with the mechanic. Writing the findings is the mechanic's first record and keeps its full time; removing the retyping at base is priced in sibling task 9948.
tasks.previous_blocker: The paper tech log was re-typed into the maintenance system after landing.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic tech logs replace paper logs on the aircraft.
tasks.still_hard: Turbulence and noise make tablet entry awkward in flight.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling a vibration that no gauge shows.

evidence.claim: TrustFlight Tech Log replaces the paper tech log on the aircraft.
In a two-month parallel run at one operator, the paper process had 52 errors and the TrustFlight electronic log had 1; vendor case.

assumptions: Boundary: from the test flight to findings logged; defect repair is outside.
Input contract: electronic tech log approved for the fleet; fallback is the paper log.
Monitoring and adjusting do not change.
s3 is the first record of the findings in the technical log and keeps its full time; transferring it to the repair log is cut in sibling task 9948.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No saving in this task: monitoring, adjusting and the first record of findings stay with the mechanic.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The aircraft mechanic keeps fitting, modifying, checking parts and adjusting in flight; phone calls, paper job cards and re-typed logs shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A mechanic with more time on the aircraft.
